panels.title: Queue depth by queue
panels.description: Every queue in BOTH runtimes: Celery's ingest, embed, crawl, evaluate, maintenance and Laravel's ai-dispatch, notify, maintenance, exports. The label is the queue NAME, never a connection name — `valkey` and `valkey-long` are Laravel connections carrying two queues each, and labelling by connection merges two backlogs so a wedged `exports` hides behind a healthy `maintenance`. `maintenance` exists in both runtimes and is disambiguated by `service`.

panels.title: Ingestion jobs by file_type and outcome
panels.description: file_type is a fixed enum from the supported-format list with everything else folded to `other` — a tenant-supplied extension is not a label value.

panels.title: Ingestion stage duration, p95 by stage and file_type (seconds)
panels.description: Which of the 17 stages is slow, for which format. The stage list is the safe retry boundaries plus their substages: acquire, validate, hash, store, parse, ocr, normalize, clean, enrich, chunk, embed, sparse, upsert, verify, activate, retire, invalidate.

panels.title: Ingestion retries by stage and error_class
panels.description: Retries climbing against a flat success rate is the fingerprint of a PERMANENT error misfiled as temporary — it retries to the attempt cap, lands in failed_jobs, and an operator retries it again.

panels.title: Pages ingested per minute by file_type
panels.description: Pages per minute is a rate() expression, deliberately: the counter stores events so the window can be changed and the series summed. A stored per-minute rate can be neither re-windowed nor added.

panels.title: OCR pages by engine and disposition
panels.description: disposition, NOT outcome: an OCR page is success, partial or error, and a partially-OCR'd page is a real third result rather than a failure. A family whose results are not the shared four names its label disposition so it cannot silently fall outside the error-rate matcher.

panels.title: Embedded chunks per second by model and kind
panels.description: kind is dense or sparse — one document produces both, from one model.

panels.title: Embedding batch duration, p95 (seconds)
panels.description: One metric for two budgets: the 5 s query-embedding budget on the chat path and the ingestion batch cost. They are the same operation at different batch sizes, which is why they share an instrument.

panels.title: Vector upsert duration, p95 by collection (seconds)
panels.description: collection is bounded — one per embedding model, shared across tenants. Tenant separation inside a collection is the four mandatory payload filters, not a collection per org.

panels.title: Vector points written vs failed
panels.description: Pairs with the verification count: Qdrant is a derived index, so a failed upsert is recoverable from stored normalized chunks and is not data loss.

panels.title: Source version publications
panels.description: Active-version pointer switches versus verification failures. A version becomes searchable only after it is fully indexed and verified; the previous version serves until then, so a failure here is invisible to users and must not be invisible here.

panels.title: Crawl runs by outcome
panels.description: Run-level success. Per-PAGE results live on kb_crawl_pages_total with a disposition label, deliberately kept apart from this.

panels.title: Crawl pages by disposition
panels.description: disposition, NOT outcome — six per-page results: discovered, changed, unchanged, skipped, missing, failed. Two of those are failures that are not in the shared four, so an `outcome` label here would place every crawl failure outside the error-rate matcher and the error rate would read healthy while pages fail.

panels.title: Crawl responses by status_class
panels.description: status_class is 2xx, 3xx, 4xx, 5xx or network. Never the host and never the URL: a crawl target set is tenant-controlled and therefore unbounded, and a URL label is the fastest way to take the metrics backend down.

panels.title: Crawl rejections by reason (robots and SSRF guard)
panels.description: The guard rejects for all eight reasons — robots, scheme, credentials, dns, private_ip, redirect, content_type, size — and an enum missing one sends those rejections to no counter at all, so the SSRF guard looks quieter than it is.

panels.title: Per-URL fetch duration, p95 (seconds)
panels.description: Against the 20 s per-URL timeout. A p95 pressed against 20 s means the crawl is spending its run budget on timeouts rather than pages.

panels.title: Crawl run duration, p95 (seconds)
panels.description: Whole-run duration, on the job-duration bucket set (1 s to 900 s). Read alongside the crawl queue depth on this dashboard: long runs plus a growing queue is a concurrency problem, long runs alone is a target problem.
